forces.title: Emergence of Digital Advertisements as a high-growth arena
forces.description: Digital advertisements are identified by McKinsey as a potential future "arena" of competition, exhibiting exceptional growth and competitive dynamism over the next 15 years. This implies a significant structural shift in where value is created and captured within the broader digital economy, leading to new strategic considerations for companies operating in or adjacent to the digital advertising and ad tech space (SE09 IN090302).
forces.source_title: Strategy in the age of arenas

forces.title: AI-driven shift in telecom operating cost structure
forces.description: The operating cost structure for telecom operators (SE09 IG0901, IG0902) is expected to undergo significant shifts due to AI adoption over the next three to five years. AI agents are becoming embedded across customer care, network operations, software engineering, and enterprise functions, leading to "tokens" accounting for a growing share of operating expenditures. This transition leads to an "agentic operating model" with approximately 20-30% AI agent and token costs.
forces.source_title: AI in Telecom: The Opex Reckoning

forces.title: Cost-creep risk from unmanaged AI scaling in telcos
forces.description: A significant risk for telecom operators (SE09 IG0901, IG0902) is the potential for "cost-creep" if AI is scaled without proactive cost management. This scenario involves simply adding token costs to an already heavy legacy operating cost base, without proportional gains in productivity, customer experience, or growth. Cost traps include accumulating bigger bills from cheaper AI models, bolting AI onto existing legacy processes, and mistaking demos for actual transformative implementation.
forces.source_title: AI in Telecom: The Opex Reckoning

forces.title: Ireland's tech hub status drives innovation and investment in Telecoms
forces.description: Ireland's strong position as a leading European technology hub, coupled with government support for digital innovation, creates a significant tailwind for the Telecoms sub-sector within Communication Services (SE09). This environment fosters continuous investment in innovation and technological change, which is crucial for market participants in areas like network infrastructure, mobile, and broadband services to remain competitive and enhance efficiency.

forces.title: Global shifts in tech strategy risk Irish Telecoms supply chains
forces.description: The Irish Telecoms sector within Communication Services (SE09) faces a key risk from potential shifts in global strategies by major multinational technology companies. These shifts include US tariff developments, reshoring initiatives, and multinational investment decisions. Such changes could negatively affect supply chains, hiring activity, and future capital expenditure in Ireland, posing challenges to the growth and operational stability of communication services providers.

forces.title: AI bifurcates M&A valuations in Technology, Media, Telecoms
forces.description: AI is creating a significant bifurcation in M&A valuations within the Technology, Media, and Telecommunications sector (including SE09). Infrastructure-layer assets like data centers, computing, and power command extraordinary valuations due to visible demand under contract, while application-layer companies are experiencing valuation corrections. This dynamic is shifting M&A activity, with rigorous diligence needed to distinguish genuine AI capabilities from mere enthusiasm and to price assets accordingly.
forces.source_title: Mid-2026 M&A Insights: AI Drives a Recovery, but Questions Remain

viewpoints.title: AI scaling risks cost-creep for telcos without proactive management
viewpoints.description: Bain notes that while AI offers transformation potential, telecom operators risk simply adding token costs to their heavy legacy operating base if they don't proactively manage costs and redesign processes. The emergence of an "agentic operating model" suggests a 70-30 split between legacy and AI costs, with AI automating or augmenting work across customer care, network operations, software engineering, and enterprise functions. This highlights the critical need for telcos to avoid cost traps like bolting AI onto existing processes or mistaking demos for full transformation, to achieve proportional productivity gains.
viewpoints.source_title: AI in Telecom: The Opex Reckoning

viewpoints.title: Ireland's Telecoms benefit from stable conditions and innovation investment
viewpoints.description: Allianz Ireland views the broader Computers & Telecoms sector, including telecom services and infrastructure, as low risk in Ireland. It maintains stable trading conditions and strong underlying performance, with low insolvencies. The sector, a key technology hub, benefits from ongoing investment in innovation and efficiency-driven technological change, supported by robust local talent demand and multinational operations. This positive environment for technology also underpins the resilience and growth potential for communication services in Ireland.

viewpoints.title: Technology, Media, Telecoms M&A sentiment lowest despite high deal value
viewpoints.description: BCG reports the Technology, Media, and Telecommunications sector has the lowest M&A sentiment rating (52) despite leading in first-half deal value. This paradox reflects buyers' aggressive investment in AI while questioning AI-driven valuations and the sustainability of the capital cycle. Traditional software-as-a-service models are under particular pressure from AI disruption. The market bifurcation sees infrastructure-layer assets (data centers, computing, power) commanding high valuations, while application-layer companies face valuation corrections, signaling a potential shift in M&A activity.
viewpoints.source_title: Mid-2026 M&A Insights: AI Drives a Recovery, but Questions Remain
